title: Building a Delta Lake with Azure Synapse Analytics
subtitle: Implementing an end-to-end ACID lakehouse pipeline on ADLS Gen2 converting raw batch streams to Parquet with deduplication and SQL external tables.
overview: Modern organizations require unified architectures to handle massive analytical ingest without compromising data integrity or concurrency. Delta Lake introduces an open-source storage abstraction that brings ACID transactional semantics, metadata scalability, and time travel to object stores. This technical guide documents our end-to-end implementation in Azure Synapse Analytics, transforming raw CSV inputs into an enterprise-ready Delta Lake with external SQL tables.
problem: Handling streaming and batch file uploads directly on cloud blob storage exposes analytics pipelines to partial reads, schema drifts, and duplicate transactions. Traditional raw data lakes lack transactional isolation: concurrent writes can leave tables in inconsistent states, and query engines frequently struggle with partition pruning when dealing with large volumes of small uncompressed CSV files.

implementation.title: 1. ADLS Gen2 Storage Hierarchy Setup
implementation.description: Established segregated storage directories separating ingestion from analytical surfaces. Raw landing zones receive untrusted batch CSV files, while the analytical output container hosts Parquet files governed by Delta transaction logs.
implementation.code:
# Storage Architecture Structure
# adls-gen2://arogyaanalytics-default/
#   ├── raw-input/
#   │   └── appointments/*.csv
#   └── lakehouse-output/
#       └── appointments_delta/
#           ├── _delta_log/
#           └── part-*.parquet

implementation.title: 2. Data Flow Design: Ingestion, Transformation & Deduplication
implementation.description: Constructed an automated Synapse Studio Data Flow using three core stages: Source (reading raw CSVs with wildcard path matching), AlterRow (applying data hygiene rules and primary key deduplication), and Sink (writing Delta Lake files).
implementation.code:
/* Synapse Data Flow Script Representation */
source(output(
    appointmentId as string,
    patientId as string,
    doctorCode as string,
    sessionTimestamp as timestamp,
    feeAmount as decimal(18,2)
  ),
  allowSchemaDrift: true,
  validateSchema: false,
  wildcardPaths: ['appointments/*.csv']) ~> sourceCSV

sourceCSV alterRow(
  upsertIf(true()) // Enforces idempotent write semantics during merge
) ~> AlterRowDeduplicate

AlterRowDeduplicate sink(allowSchemaDrift: true,
  validateSchema: false,
  format: 'delta',
  compressionType: 'snappy',
  vacuum: 0,
  deletable: false,
  insertable: true,
  updateable: false,
  upsertable: true,
  keys: ['appointmentId'],
  skipDuplicateMapInputs: true,
  skipDuplicateMapOutputs: true) ~> sinkDelta

implementation.title: 3. Sink Optimization and Performance Tuning
implementation.description: Configured the Delta sink for columnar writes with snappy compression, enabled 'Optimize Write' to reduce small-file fragmentation, and set copy behavior to 'Flatten hierarchy' for standard lakehouse directory layouts.
implementation.code:
-- Optimization settings configured in Synapse pipeline:
-- Optimize Write: Enabled (auto-compacts small batches into target ~128MB Parquet files)
-- Format: Delta (Snappy compression)
-- Hierarchy: Flattened structure for efficient partition pruning

implementation.title: 4. External Table Creation for Serverless SQL Analytics
implementation.description: Exposed the underlying Delta files through Synapse Serverless SQL Pools using external tables, allowing reporting tools and BI dashboards to execute ANSI SQL queries directly against the lakehouse.
implementation.code:
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE analytics.appointments_delta (
    appointmentId VARCHAR(64),
    patientId VARCHAR(64),
    doctorCode VARCHAR(32),
    sessionTimestamp DATETIME2,
    feeAmount DECIMAL(18,2)
)
WITH (
    LOCATION = 'lakehouse-output/appointments_delta/',
    DATA_SOURCE = SynapseDeltaDataSource,
    FILE_FORMAT = DeltaFileFormat
);

impact: Eliminated data corruption from concurrent batch writes via Delta Lake ACID transaction guarantees.
Drastically accelerated analytical query speeds by moving from row-oriented uncompressed CSV to columnar Snappy-compressed Parquet.
Enabled BI dashboards to run real-time ANSI SQL queries via Synapse Serverless SQL external tables without spinning up dedicated data warehouses.
lessons: Always enable 'Optimize Write' in Synapse Data Flows to prevent the classic small-file problem when streaming or micro-batching into Delta sinks.
Configure fine-grained RBAC on ADLS Gen2 storage accounts: separate ingest identity credentials from analytical query engine service principals.
